dedupe_keys.name: serdux marcim agent based simulation of cyberattack propagation in maritime critical infrastructure netlogo and python

description: SERDUX-MARCIM simulates how a cyberattack spreads across the computing network of an organisation in the maritime sector, as the agent-based part of the MARCIM framework for modelling maritime cyber defence. The CoMSES Net release read on 2026-09-28 (version 0.0.1, published 20 August 2026) treats every asset, from servers, endpoints, routers and gateways to vessel systems and radars, as an agent in one of six states: susceptible, exposed, resistant, degraded, unavailable or destroyed. Each agent is updated not by a behavioural rule but by six ordinary differential equations with eight time-dependent rates, derived from the capabilities of the defender and the attacker and the degree and duration of the attack through a cyber risk approach aligned with the OWASP risk rating method. It is written in NetLogo and Python. Access is free download under the LGPL-3.0 licence. Caveats: it is an early release with few downloads, and the rates rest on expert scoring, not incident data. It supports cascading failure studies of port and shipping IT, such as comparing recovery and sanitation strategies. No related maritime cyber model is catalogued.
inputs: organisation network of servers, endpoints, routers, gateways, vessel systems and radars
name: SERDUX-MARCIM: agent-based simulation of cyberattack propagation in maritime critical infrastructure (NetLogo and Python)
outputs: state trajectories of assets (susceptible, exposed, resistant, degraded, unavailable, destroyed)
provider: Diego Edison Cabuya Padilla, Carlos A. Castañeda-Marroquín and Daniel Díaz-López (CoMSES Net)

sources.note: read (CoMSES JSON): version 0.0.1, published 20 August 2026, LGPL-3.0, NetLogo and Python; simulates cyberattack propagation over the computing network of a maritime organisation at the strategic level; instantiation of ABM-MARCIM; each asset (servers, endpoints, routers, gateways, vessel systems, radars) is in one of six states; 13 admissible transitions; local update is a system of six ODEs with eight time-dependent rates derived from organisation and attacker capabilities and attack degree and duration via a cyber risk approach aligned with OWASP Risk Rating; references MARCIM papers in DYNA 2024

title_en: SERDUX-MARCIM: agent-based simulation of cyberattack propagation in maritime critical infrastructure (NetLogo and Python)
